Export a SpatialData points element to punkst transcript format

Source: R/export.R
sdata_export.Rd

Runs the bundled spatialdata_to_punkst.py with system2(); no Python module is loaded into R. The output is a tab-separated file with a #-prefixed header and columns x, y, feature, ready for punkst pts2tiles.

Usage

sdata_export(
  sdata,
  out,
  points_key = "transcripts",
  coordinate_system = "intrinsic",
  min_qv = NULL,
  qv_column = "qv",
  feature_column = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  python = NULL,
  log = paste0(out, ".export.log")
)

Arguments

sdata

Path to the SpatialData .zarr store.

out

Output path (.tsv or .tsv.gz).

points_key

Name of the points element.

coordinate_system

Coordinate system to export in, or "intrinsic" for the stored coordinates. NULL lets the script infer it when only one is registered.

min_qv

Drop rows with quality below this value (e.g. 20 for Xenium).

qv_column

Name of the quality column.

feature_column

Feature column; default is the element's feature key.

overwrite

Re-export if out already exists.

python

Interpreter override; see punkst_setup().

log

Log file for the script's output.

Value

The output path, invisibly.

Details

For Xenium stores written by spatialdata-io, the stored coordinates are microns while the registered global coordinate system is image pixels, so the default coordinate_system = "intrinsic" exports microns as punkst expects.

Examples

# Requires a Python interpreter with spatialdata; skipped otherwise.
store <- file.path(tempdir(), "demo.zarr")
dir.create(store)
tryCatch(
    sdata_export(store, tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")),
    error = function(e) message("spatialdata not available: ", conditionMessage(e)))
